jsonld.description: Mobile app design, development and measurement for brands with repeat use.

acceptedAnswer.text: Mobile app development is the work of designing and building an app that gives customers a reason to return on their phones, and measuring whether it does.

mainEntity.name: How does mobile app development work with MMC?

acceptedAnswer.text: We first check that an app beats a mobile website for your customers, then design the core journey, build for speed and reliability, instrument key events and improve it after launch.

mainEntity.name: What does mobile app development cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: We quote per project, after a call, once the scope is clear: what you need, how much of it, and what it has to connect to. The scope and the fee are agreed in writing before work starts.
No. We cannot guarantee installs or usage. We commit to an honest view of whether you need an app, a tested design, a stable build and measurement from day one.

mainEntity.name: Who is mobile app development for?

acceptedAnswer.text: Brands whose customers will use an app repeatedly. Not only D2C. We work with D2C, B2B and education brands, and set the work up differently for each: D2C on reorders and loyalty, B2B on tools teams use every day, education on portals for students and parents.

mainEntity.name: What do you need from us?

acceptedAnswer.text: A clear description of the repeat use, your brand assets, your existing systems and data, and a decision-maker for each stage.

leaks.lede: An app is a long commitment. Each stage below is where apps go wrong, and how we run it.

stages.breaks: Building an app because competitors have one.
stages.why: An app has real costs, and it only pays if customers use it repeatedly. A fast website is often enough.
stages.does: We compare an app with a mobile website against your customers' habits, and tell you if an app is not worth it yet.

stages.breaks: Packing in every feature at launch.
stages.why: Apps that try to do everything do the main thing poorly, and users leave.
stages.does: We design the one journey customers return for, and keep the first release focused.

stages.breaks: Shipping a slow or unstable first version.
stages.why: A poor first experience is hard to recover from, since many users do not return.
stages.does: We build for speed and stability, with testing on the phones your customers actually use.

stages.why: Without events and retention data you cannot tell what to fix.
stages.does: We instrument key events and retention from the first release, and connect them to your marketing data.

stages.breaks: Treating launch as the finish line.
stages.why: Store presence and regular releases decide whether an app is found and keeps improving.
stages.does: We prepare the store listing, plan releases and use what we learn to improve the app.
